How much does transmission replacement cost?

A full transmission replacement — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$6,238–$6,764

Labor $1,127–$1,654 · parts ~$5,110

Bay Area: no published metro-specific figure found — the national range is the honest reference.

Why quotes run $1,500 to $8,000+

Unit type
Used: $1,500–$3,500 installed, no warranty. Remanufactured: $2,500–$5,500. New OEM: $4,000–$7,000+.
Transmission type
CVTs and European units run highest — a BMW X5 rebuild alone can pass $5,000. A Camry's sits at the other end.
Labor
Replacement labor runs $1,127–$1,654 nationally — 6–12 hours. A rebuild takes 15–40. Get the labor line itemized, not bundled.
What else is worn
Torque converters add $600–$1,500; control modules $897–$969. A cheap quote that skips these isn't cheap.
Rebuild vs. replace

What the extra money buys

Rebuild
$1,500–$3,500

Your case, new internals. Cheaper when the damage is moderate and the case is sound. Warranty is usually shorter — 12–24 months.

Remanufactured replacement
$2,500–$5,500

Factory-reman unit with a 24–36 month warranty. The safer bet on high-mileage cars or when the case itself is suspect.

Bottom line: rebuild the devil you know when damage is moderate; replace when it's catastrophic or the car has 150k+ miles. And do the math against the car's value first.

Common questions

Rebuild or replace — which is better?

Rebuild when the case is sound and damage is moderate — it's cheaper. Replace with remanufactured when damage is severe or mileage is high; the warranty is better.

How long does it take?

A replacement is 6–12 hours of labor but 3–5 days in the shop with scheduling. A rebuild is a week or more — the unit sits apart on a bench.

Is my car worth it?

Compare the quote to the car's value. A $5,000 transmission in a $6,000 car only makes sense if the rest of the car is solid and you're keeping it.

What are the warning signs?

Slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, grinding, and leaking red fluid. A fluid service ($150–$400) sometimes helps early — once it's slipping badly, it won't.

Every car prices differently.

The range above is a national average. Your price depends on the unit, the transmission type, and what's worn besides. Take a photo of your estimate in Brightglow for a second opinion on the actual car.
